clue.text: Reportedly US money may possibly secure rock

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the phrase before the definition is to be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: US money is the dollar, and may possibly is might: together dollar might

explanation.surface: A speculator wonders whether American cash could buy up a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' says DOLLAR MIGHT is heard, and spoken quickly it gives the rock's name; 'secure' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolomite is a sedimentary rock made of calcium magnesium carbonate, giving its name to the Dolomites.

clue.text: Security one's set up' in storehouse

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits within the storehouse word

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the letters are raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: one's is I'S, one plus the verb is

explanation.surface: Someone stows their valuables away in a warehouse for safe keeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Security' is the definition, in the sense of money handed over as a guarantee. The stray apostrophe after 'up' is a print mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is money handed over as security, against loss or damage.

clue.text: Endless need for transparent resin

indicators.note: endless says the word for need loses its final letter

parts.note: need means lack

explanation.surface: Someone requires a clear resin for a finishing job.
explanation.definitionFit: Lac is the resinous secretion of an Asian insect, used to make shellac varnish.

clue.text: Sadly served disheartened lady with second lot of tea

indicators.note: served with signals that the trimmed lady is placed after the tea pieces

parts.note: mo is a moment or second
an urnful is as much tea as an urn holds

indicators.note: disheartened means the word lady loses its middle letters, its heart

explanation.surface: A dispirited woman is cheered with a second round of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes AD from the middle of LADY, leaving LY, which joins MO and URNFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To act mournfully is to act in a grieving, sorrowful way, which is what sadly describes.

clue.text: Time taken to stop noisy rabble upset teacher

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken to stop puts the time letter on top of what follows
upset in a down clue turns the letters upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: a rout is an old word for a disorderly crowd or rabble

explanation.surface: A teacher gets upset when a rowdy class is finally quietened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ROUT to UTOR, and T is put on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher, or one who teaches small groups at a university.

clue.text: Dispatch racehorse from East to West

indicators.note: in an across clue, east to west means read from right to left

parts.note: Red Rum was the famous horse that won the Grand National three times

explanation.surface: A racehorse is shipped across the country from east to west.
explanation.walkthrough: RED RUM won Britain's Grand National steeplechase in 1973, 1974 and 1977; 'from East to West' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch someone is a euphemism for killing them, so it is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Foolish person holding up high-class domestic fixture

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up means the foolish person is underneath, supporting the high-class letter

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage
a nit is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot struggles to lift a posh household fitting into place.
explanation.walkthrough: U means upper-class in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a fitted kitchen cupboard, a typical fixture in a home.

clue.text: Feebleness of American guy accepting fake receipt

indicators.note: accepting means the guy takes the other letters inside him

parts.note: dude is American slang for a man

indicators.note: fake means the letters of receipt are falsified into a new order

explanation.surface: An American man is too weak to see through a forged receipt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fake' rearranges RECEIPT to ECREPIT, which DUDE is 'accepting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepitude is the weakness that comes with old age or long use.

clue.text: Book store

definitions.meaning: to book a seat is to set it aside in advance
a store is a supply kept back for later use

explanation.definitionFit: To reserve is to book; a reserve is a stock held back, a store.

clue.text: Temper Capone displayed at certain time of year

parts.note: to season is to temper or moderate
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: Gangster Al Capone shows his bad temper once a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seasonal occurs or is available only at a particular time of the year.

clue.text: Gradually master the music and return to normality

definitions.meaning: a musician learns pieces of music bit by bit
to restore life to normal after a disaster

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to restore order after a setback, and literally a musician learns compositions.

clue.text: In which a pouty daughter becomes a doughty porter

definitions.text: In which a pouty daughter becomes a doughty porter

parts.words: In which a pouty daughter becomes a doughty porter
parts.note: swapping the first sounds of pouty and daughter gives doughty and porter, the classic slip of the tongue named after a Warden of New College, Oxford

explanation.surface: A sulky girl turns into a brave carrier of luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the transposition of initial sounds between words, as in the clue's example.

clue.text: Ubiquitous ' person met in resort

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, to sort these letters again

explanation.surface: Someone you keep bumping into at a holiday resort seems to be everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' as re-sort rearranges PERSON MET IN. The stray apostrophe is a print mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnipresent means present everywhere at once, so it is a direct synonym of ubiquitous.

clue.text: He succeeds in producing vocal melody

indicators.note: producing vocal tells us the melody word is voiced, giving its sound

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A singer makes it big by performing a tuneful song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He succeeds' is the definition: an heir is one who succeeds to a title.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is the person who succeeds to an estate or throne on another's death.

clue.text: Plant little fellow with soldiers in street

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: titch is British slang for a small person
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers

explanation.surface: A small man marches with troops down a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitchwort is a white-flowered wild plant of hedgerows, once used for a stitch in the side.

clue.text: Removal of locks certainly not given backing at first

indicators.note: at first places the reversed word at the front
given backing means the word is turned to read backwards

parts.note: sure means certainly

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to back a plan to cut their hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' suggests doors and keys, but here means hair, as shaved from a monk's crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaving of a monk's crown, a deliberate removal of hair.

clue.text: Turning tail, join vessel below warehouse

indicators.note: in a down clue, below puts the vessel underneath
turning tail means only the final pair of letters of the join word swap round

parts.note: to enter is to join, as in entering a competition
a pot is a vessel

explanation.surface: A cowardly sailor turns back from his ship at the dockside store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning tail' swaps the last two letters of ENTER, giving ENTRE; 'below' puts POT under it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepot is a trading port or warehouse where goods are stored before re-export.

clue.text: Compound Revere took from Boston to Lexington, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the description is spoken aloud

parts.words: Revere took from Boston to Lexington
parts.note: Paul Revere's famous journey on horseback in 1775 was a midnight ride

explanation.surface: A question about the route a patriot took between two Massachusetts towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Revere rode from Boston to Lexington at night to warn that British troops were coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitride is a chemical compound of nitrogen with a more electropositive element.

clue.text: Relief to high-flyer, one involved in business plan

parts.note: Co is short for company, a business

indicators.note: involved in means the one sits inside the plan

parts.note: a plot is a plan
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A high-powered executive is relieved to be included in the business plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A second pilot relieves the captain of an aircraft, someone who flies high.

clue.text: Anxiety about old politician's quality

indicators.note: about means the anxiety word goes round the other

parts.note: care is worry or anxiety
Lib is short for a Liberal, a member of the old British party

explanation.surface: Concern grows about an elderly MP's standard of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Calibre is quality or standard, as in a person of high calibre.

clue.text: English abstainer's taken in fish salad

indicators.note: taken in means these letters go inside the fish

parts.note: luce is an old name for the pike
TT, teetotal, describes one who abstains from drink

explanation.surface: An English teetotaller tucks into a fish salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettuce is the leafy plant that forms the basis of most green salads.

clue.text: Beg to be given directions before parley

indicators.note: before means the directions come first

parts.note: E and N are the compass directions east and north
to treat is to negotiate or parley

explanation.surface: Someone pleads for guidance before negotiations open.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to ask earnestly or beg.

clue.text: National emblem embodying general and king

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A country's symbol depicts a military leader alongside the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The leek is the national emblem of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The leek is worn on St David's Day as the emblem of Wales.

definitions.meaning: the answer to 6 is a military body, and this word is one such body
the answer to 8 in its sense of aloofness or reticence

explanation.walkthrough: 6 is UNIT and 8 is RESERVE: a detachment is a unit of troops, and detachment is reserve of manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Detachment is both a body of troops sent off on duty and emotional aloofness.

clue.text: A Scandinavian nomad's rising dismay

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: a Lapp is a reindeer-herding nomad of northern Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A northern herder's fortunes go up, much to someone's dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to fill with horror or dismay, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Craggy outcrop shows sign of damage

definitions.meaning: a steep rocky cliff or outcrop on a hillside
a mark left on skin or a surface after injury

explanation.definitionFit: A scar is both a steep rock face and the mark a healed wound leaves.

clue.text: No union would follow such legal action

definitions.text: No union would follow such legal action

parts.words: No union would follow such legal action
parts.note: a lawsuit brought when an engagement is broken off, after which no marriage takes place

explanation.surface: A trade dispute in court leaves the workers without a union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks like a trade union, but here means a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The old legal action was brought by a jilted fiance when a promise to marry was broken.

clue.text: Carbon that's deposited around diamonds

indicators.note: deposited around means the letters are laid round the carbon symbol

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Carbon is laid down around the precious stones in the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds' is the definition: ice is slang for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is underworld slang for diamonds, from their glittering clear look.

clue.text: Complete set of books printed in republic

indicators.note: printed in means the books go inside the republic word

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A complete collection of books is published in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole or complete, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Least exciting examination of living quarters

parts.note: a flat is a set of rooms to live in
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: An inspection of someone's apartment proves the dullest of jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattest means dullest or most lacking in excitement, the superlative of flat.
